parsed.stack: iOS 18+ both sides, Swift 6 / SwiftUI + ActivityKit + WidgetKit. Interactive Live Activity button backed by an App Intent; ActivityKit push-to-start and push-update tokens. Backend is a small Go service on Fly.io (~$25/mo) holding household pairing, the confirmation ledger and APNs token registry, Postgres for the ledger. Portal letter summarisation uses the on-device Foundation Model first and a frontier text model as fallback for long PDFs (about 6k in / 600 out per letter). EventKit for the shared calendar, HKClinicalType/FHIR read on the adult child's own device. App Store only.
milestones: Week 1-3: ActivityKit spike. Push-to-start plus push-update to a second device, interactive button wired to an App Intent, and a 500-event latency and survival log. Measures both the 60-second delivery kill and how long an activity actually stays on the lock screen.
Week 4-6: Pairing and ledger. Two-household invite flow, confirmation write path, conflict handling when both households act, and the single-line shared state view.

Week 7-9: Parent-side onboarding. The whole product dies here if an 80-year-old cannot complete setup, so this is a full sprint on a one-screen install, notification and Live Activity permission flow, remotely assisted by the adult child.
Week 10-12: Medication schedule entry, missed-dose state, EventKit appointment writes, and the HealthKit clinical records read for appointment changes.
Week 13-15: Portal letter summarisation, on-device first with cloud fallback, plus subscription paywall and privacy policy / health-data counsel review.
Week 16-17: 20-household closed beta, 4.5.3 review-notes dry run, submission.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That a Live Activity can be the always-visible two-household surface at all, when iOS caps an activity's life at roughly 8 hours on screen (12 hours before forced dismissal) and budget-throttles push updates, so the 'shared, always-visible surface' degrades to a widget within a day unless something re-starts it, and every re-start is another push that may be throttled.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Ship a throwaway TestFlight build to five paired devices that push-starts an activity and pushes an update every 20 minutes for 14 days, logging on-screen survival and delivery latency - two days of work and the $99 developer account.
